title: Standard Form (Scientific Notation)
description: Write and calculate with numbers in standard form.

notes.heading: What is Standard Form?

illustration.alt: Diagram showing a number written in standard form as 3.4 times 10 to the power 5, with the coefficient, base, and exponent labelled.
illustration.caption: Standard form writes a number as a coefficient between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of 10.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
Standard form (also called scientific notation) is a way of writing very large or very small numbers compactly. A number is in standard form when it is written as:
$$a \times 10^n$$
where $1 \leq a < 10$ and $n$ is an integer.

🔑 Key Concept
The coefficient $a$ is always at least $1$ and less than $10$. The power of $10$ tells you how many places to move the decimal point.

💡 Worked Example
Write $340\,000$ in standard form.

Step 1: Place the decimal point after the first non-zero digit to get $3.4$.

Step 2: Count how many places the decimal point has moved from its original position.
$$340\,000 \rightarrow 3.40000$$
The decimal point moved $5$ places to the left.

Step 3: Write the answer.
$$340\,000 = 3.4 \times 10^5$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Standard form makes large and small numbers easier to read and compare.
• The coefficient must satisfy $1 \leq a < 10$.
• The exponent $n$ is positive for large numbers and negative for small numbers.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Writing $34 \times 10^4$ instead of $3.4 \times 10^5$. The coefficient $34$ is not between $1$ and $10$, so this is not standard form.

notes.heading: The Coefficient
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The coefficient in standard form is the number $a$ in $a \times 10^n$. It must be greater than or equal to $1$ and less than $10$.

🔑 Key Concept
To find the coefficient, move the decimal point in the original number so that only one non-zero digit is to the left of the decimal point.

💡 Worked Example
What is the coefficient when $5\,600$ is written in standard form?

Move the decimal point three places to the left:
$$5\,600 = 5.6 \times 10^3$$
The coefficient is $5.6$.

💡 Worked Example
What is the coefficient when $0.0072$ is written in standard form?

Move the decimal point three places to the right:
$$0.0072 = 7.2 \times 10^{-3}$$
The coefficient is $7.2$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $a = 1$ is allowed, but $a = 10$ is not.
• $0.5 \times 10^4$ is not standard form because $0.5 < 1$.
• $12 \times 10^4$ is not standard form because $12 \geq 10$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Leaving the coefficient as a whole number, such as $45 \times 10^2$. Always adjust so that $1 \leq a < 10$.

notes.heading: Positive Powers of 10 for Large Numbers
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A positive power of $10$ represents a large number. The exponent tells you how many zeros follow the $1$.

🔑 Key Concept
$$10^n = 1 \underbrace{00\dots0}_{n \text{ zeros}}$$
For example:
$$10^2 = 100, \quad 10^3 = 1\,000, \quad 10^6 = 1\,000\,000$$

💡 Worked Example
Write $7\,200\,000$ in standard form.

Step 1: Move the decimal point to after the first digit:
$$7.200\,000$$

Step 2: Count the moves. The decimal point moved $6$ places to the left, so the exponent is $6$.

Step 3: Write the answer:
$$7\,200\,000 = 7.2 \times 10^6$$

✅ Check
$7.2 \times 10^6 = 7.2 \times 1\,000\,000 = 7\,200\,000$. Correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Large numbers have positive exponents.
• The exponent equals the number of places the decimal point moves to the left.
• $10^0 = 1$, so any number between $1$ and $10$ is already in standard form with $n = 0$.

notes.heading: Negative Powers of 10 for Small Numbers
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A negative power of $10$ represents a small number between $0$ and $1$. The exponent tells you how many places the decimal point is to the right of $1$.

🔑 Key Concept
$$10^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{10^n}$$
For example:
$$10^{-1} = 0.1, \quad 10^{-3} = 0.001, \quad 10^{-6} = 0.000\,001$$

💡 Worked Example
Write $0.000\,083$ in standard form.

Step 1: Move the decimal point to after the first non-zero digit:
$$8.3$$

Step 2: Count the moves. The decimal point moved $5$ places to the right, so the exponent is $-5$.

Step 3: Write the answer:
$$0.000\,083 = 8.3 \times 10^{-5}$$

✅ Check
$8.3 \times 10^{-5} = 8.3 \times 0.000\,01 = 0.000\,083$. Correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Small numbers (between $0$ and $1$) have negative exponents.
• The size of the negative exponent tells you how many places the decimal point moves to the right.
• A negative exponent does not make the answer negative; it makes the value small.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Writing $0.83 \times 10^{-4}$ for $0.000\,083$. The coefficient must be at least $1$, so the correct form is $8.3 \times 10^{-5}$.

notes.heading: Converting from Ordinary Numbers to Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To convert an ordinary number to standard form, adjust the decimal point to produce a coefficient between $1$ and $10$, then use the correct power of $10$.

🔑 How it works
1. Find the first non-zero digit.
2. Place the decimal point immediately after it.
3. Count how many places you moved the decimal point.
4. Use a positive exponent if you moved left; use a negative exponent if you moved right.

💡 Worked Example
Write $456\,000$ in standard form.

Step 1: The first digit is $4$, so the coefficient starts as $4.56$.

Step 2: The decimal point moved $5$ places to the left.

Step 3: Write the answer:
$$456\,000 = 4.56 \times 10^5$$

💡 Worked Example
Write $0.000\,009\,04$ in standard form.

Step 1: The first non-zero digit is $9$, so the coefficient is $9.04$.

Step 2: The decimal point moved $6$ places to the right.

Step 3: Write the answer:
$$0.000\,009\,04 = 9.04 \times 10^{-6}$$

✅ Check
$9.04 \times 10^{-6} = 9.04 \times 0.000\,001 = 0.000\,009\,04$. Correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Left moves give positive exponents.
• Right moves give negative exponents.
• Count all place moves, including those past zeros.

notes.heading: Converting from Standard Form to Ordinary Numbers
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To convert from standard form to an ordinary number, move the decimal point in the coefficient according to the exponent.

🔑 How it works
If the exponent is positive, move the decimal point to the right.
If the exponent is negative, move the decimal point to the left.

💡 Worked Example
Write $6.7 \times 10^4$ as an ordinary number.

Step 1: Start with $6.7$.

Step 2: The exponent is $4$, so move the decimal point $4$ places to the right.

Step 3: Fill any gaps with zeros:
$$6.7 \times 10^4 = 67\,000$$

💡 Worked Example
Write $2.05 \times 10^{-3}$ as an ordinary number.

Step 1: Start with $2.05$.

Step 2: The exponent is $-3$, so move the decimal point $3$ places to the left.

Step 3: Fill any gaps with zeros:
$$2.05 \times 10^{-3} = 0.002\,05$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Positive exponent: make the number larger (move right).
• Negative exponent: make the number smaller (move left).
• Add zeros as placeholders when necessary.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Moving the decimal point the wrong way. A positive exponent always produces a larger ordinary number, never a smaller one.

notes.heading: Multiplying and Dividing in Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To multiply or divide numbers in standard form, handle the coefficients and the powers of $10$ separately.

🔑 How it works
Multiplication:
$$(a \times 10^m) \times (b \times 10^n) = (a \times b) \times 10^{m+n}$$

Division:
$$(a \times 10^m) \div (b \times 10^n) = \left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right) \times 10^{m-n}$$

After calculating, check that the final coefficient is still between $1$ and $10$.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Multiplication
Simplify $(2 \times 10^3) \times (3 \times 10^5)$.

Step 1: Multiply the coefficients:
$$2 \times 3 = 6$$

Step 2: Add the exponents:
$$10^3 \times 10^5 = 10^{3+5} = 10^8$$

Step 3: Combine:
$$(2 \times 10^3) \times (3 \times 10^5) = 6 \times 10^8$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Division
Simplify $(8 \times 10^7) \div (2 \times 10^4)$.

Step 1: Divide the coefficients:
$$8 \div 2 = 4$$

Step 2: Subtract the exponents:
$$10^7 \div 10^4 = 10^{7-4} = 10^3$$

Step 3: Combine:
$$(8 \times 10^7) \div (2 \times 10^4) = 4 \times 10^3$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Multiply or divide the coefficients.
• Add exponents when multiplying; subtract exponents when dividing.
• Adjust the final answer so that the coefficient is between $1$ and $10$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding exponents during division. Remember: division means subtract the exponents.

notes.heading: Adding and Subtracting in Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To add or subtract numbers in standard form, first rewrite them so that they have the same power of $10$. Then add or subtract the coefficients.

🔑 How it works
1. Choose the larger power of $10$.
2. Rewrite the other number with the same power of $10$.
3. Add or subtract the coefficients.
4. Keep the common power of $10$.

💡 Worked Example
Simplify $(3 \times 10^4) + (5 \times 10^3)$.

Step 1: Rewrite $5 \times 10^3$ with power $10^4$.
Because $10^3 = 10^{-1} \times 10^4$, we have:
$$5 \times 10^3 = 0.5 \times 10^4$$

Step 2: Add the coefficients:
$$3 + 0.5 = 3.5$$

Step 3: Keep the power of $10$:
$$(3 \times 10^4) + (5 \times 10^3) = 3.5 \times 10^4$$

✅ Check
$3 \times 10^4 = 30\,000$ and $5 \times 10^3 = 5\,000$. Their sum is $35\,000 = 3.5 \times 10^4$. Correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• You cannot add or subtract coefficients unless the powers of $10$ are the same.
• It is usually easiest to convert to the larger power of $10$.
• Check your answer by converting to ordinary numbers.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding the coefficients directly: $3 \times 10^4 + 5 \times 10^3 \neq 8 \times 10^4$. The powers must match first.

flashcards.definition: A way of writing numbers as $a \times 10^n$ where $1 \leq a < 10$ and $n$ is an integer.
The number $a$ in the standard form $a \times 10^n$. It must be at least $1$ and less than $10$.
The number that is raised to a power in standard form; it is always $10$.
The power $n$ in $a \times 10^n$. It tells how many places the decimal point has moved.
An exponent greater than zero, used for large numbers in standard form.
An exponent less than zero, used for small numbers between $0$ and $1$.
Move the decimal point so that one non-zero digit is before it, then use the matching power of $10$.
Move the decimal point in the coefficient by the number of places given by the exponent.
Multiply the coefficients and add the exponents.
Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents.
Rewrite the numbers with the same power of $10$, then add the coefficients.
The size of a number given by the power of $10$ in its standard form.

questions.stem: Which of the following is written in correct standard form?
questions.explanation: Standard form requires the coefficient to be at least $1$ and less than $10$. Only $7.3 \times 10^2$ satisfies this condition. The other options have coefficients outside the allowed range.
Move the decimal point four places to the left to get $5.6$. Because it moved four places, the exponent is $4$, so $56\,000 = 5.6 \times 10^4$.
Move the decimal point six places to the right to get $9.2$. Because it moved six places to the right, the exponent is $-6$, so $0.000\,009\,2 = 9.2 \times 10^{-6}$.
The exponent is $5$, so move the decimal point five places to the right: $3.7 \times 10^5 = 370\,000$.
The exponent is $-4$, so move the decimal point four places to the left: $4.2 \times 10^{-4} = 0.000\,042$.
Multiply the coefficients: $3 \times 2 = 6$. Add the exponents: $10^4 \times 10^6 = 10^{10}$. So the answer is $6 \times 10^{10}$.
Divide the coefficients: $8 \div 4 = 2$. Subtract the exponents: $10^9 \div 10^3 = 10^6$. So the answer is $2 \times 10^6$.

Multiply the coefficients: $2 \times 5 = 10$. Add the exponents: $10^3 \times 10^2 = 10^5$. This gives $10 \times 10^5$, but the coefficient $10$ is not in standard form, so rewrite it as $1 \times 10^6$.
Rewrite $3 \times 10^4$ as $0.3 \times 10^5$. Then add the coefficients: $4 + 0.3 = 4.3$, giving $4.3 \times 10^5$.
$10^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{10^3} = \dfrac{1}{1000} = 0.001$. A negative exponent gives a reciprocal, not a negative number.
Move the decimal point two places to the left: $2.5 \times 10^{-2} = 0.025$.
Move the decimal point eight places to the left to get $7.2$, so $720\,000\,000 = 7.2 \times 10^8$.
Divide the coefficients: $6 \div 3 = 2$. Subtract the exponents: $10^5 \div 10^{-2} = 10^{5 - (-2)} = 10^7$. So the answer is $2 \times 10^7$.

questions.stem: A calculator display shows $7.2\text{E}6$. What ordinary number does this represent?
questions.explanation: $7.2\text{E}6$ means $7.2 \times 10^6$. Move the decimal point six places to the right: $7.2 \times 10^6 = 7\,200\,000$.
